assertion_quality_findings_non_blocking.finding: CTX-STALE-CAS-ISOLATED-FROM-PRECONDITION asserts current["revision"] != 99999 - a comparison against a literal the fixture itself chose; it cannot fail in any reachable state.

The comment says the required-field list 'is read from the schema, not from what the implementation happens to emit'. It is a hand-typed slice. I verified it against the published contract (tests/contracts/fixtures/domain.schema.json -> ContextBundle.required) and the 17 names match exactly, so the assertion is correct, but it will not track a contract change and put() already enforces the same list.

CTX-MATERIALIZE-MANIFEST-NAMES-BUNDLE-AND-RESUME checks only bundle_ref; the resume half of the name is not checked (also feeds B6). It is additionally a disjunction (`==` OR substring-of-serialization), so any mention of the bundle id anywhere satisfies it.

Inside the manifest loop, `filepath.IsAbs(full)` is always true because full is filepath.Join(ws, name) with ws absolute, so one of the three conditions in CTX-MATERIALIZE-ENTRIES-RESOLVE-UNDER-WORKSPACE adds no constraint; the escape-detection work is done entirely by the Rel/HasPrefix test.

CTX-MATERIALIZE-WORKSPACE-IS-DESTINATION-NOT-CWD probes only for a literal `inputs` directory in the process cwd. My probe of materialize.go (line 151 filepath.Abs(destination)) shows the anti-cwd property is real, but this id would not notice a leak named anything else; the load-bearing half is workspaceExists, asserted separately.

CTX-FOREIGN-WORKER-CANNOT-READ-CONTEXT is emitted only if both ProvisionPrincipal and IssueCredential succeed. Neither failure records an ok(false), so that id can vanish silently and the run still reports PASS with one fewer assertion - unlike line 264, which does record the fallback. There is no expected-count gate anywhere: tests/context/check/main.go only fails on len(failures)>0 or zero ids (main.go:108-124), so a shrunken green set is accepted.

contextPhase returns early on the first refusal, so a mid-phase product regression is reported as one failure plus a mass of silently missing ids rather than as the full set; a reviewer cannot distinguish 'this assertion regressed' from 'the phase never got there' from the id list alone. Contrast main.go's phases, which mostly record and continue.
countKind and countStaleTasks are defined and never called - dead helpers; go vet does not flag unused methods. The comment above them describes scoping the suite never uses.

CHG-STALE-BASE-STATE-REJECTED submits base_state_revision 99999, i.e. a FUTURE revision, to test staleness; it works (412 STALE_REVISION) but the assertion name promises the stale-input case and exercises an out-of-range case. The genuine stale direction is covered elsewhere (my Z9 run), so this is naming only.

CHG-CONFLICT-DOES-NOT-OVERWRITE-A-DRAFT and CHG-RESOLUTION-KEEPS-BOTH-DRAFTS compare whole serialized proposals against an in-memory snapshot captured at creation. They are honest, and the executor volunteers in progress_note_1.json that no mutation can give the first teeth; my own reading is that they would also break spuriously on any added updated_at field, so they encode 'nothing may ever touch a draft' more strictly than the domain contract states.
